notes: §1985:XIII.3.15.3 SR1: "Integer-1 and integer-2 must not exceed three significant digits in length." and neither "may be specified in such a way as to cause any line of a report group to be presented outside the vertical subdivision of the page designated for that report group type"; "Integer-2 may be zero." The subdivision half is mostly kept: ScreenReportGroupLines refuses (COBOL2199) an absolute line outside GroupLimits (SR6 c)), a body group's relative tail after an absolute line past its lower limit (SR6 d)), and a heading or footing group of relative lines outside its region; PLUS 0 is accepted. But ScreenReportLineClauses bounds the integers by ReportModel.VerticalLimit (the page limit, or 9999 unpaged: §2023:13.18.35.3 SR3) with no 85 arm, so four-digit integers compile, and a body group of relative lines only is never sized against its region (the comment defers it to the run-time fit test). Probes at 85 (work-slice-54/c6*; classes b, c, f): LINE PLUS 1000 unpaged and LINE 1000 under PAGE LIMIT 1200 run ('RAN'); LINE 3 above FIRST DETAIL 5, LINE 48 + PLUS 5 past LAST DETAIL 50, and a PAGE HEADING PLUS 4 past FIRST DETAIL 5 each print COBOL2199; a DETAIL of PLUS 1 then PLUS 50 (51 lines, region 5-50) compiles and prints BBB on line 55; PLUS 0, PLUS 0001 and LINE 0999 run; '+1' prints COBOL0900; LINE 0 prints COBOL2386. The witness (LINE 55 past LAST DETAIL 50) is refused with COBOL2199. kb/Work PB5252 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-pipe/slice-54.json).

next.reason: 1985: integer-1 and integer-2 'must not exceed three significant digits', no line may fall outside the page subdivision for its group type, and 'Integer-2 may be zero'. §2023:13.18.35.3 SR3: 'Neither integer-1 nor integer-2 shall exceed the page limit, or 9999 if the report is not divided into pages ... Integer-2 may be zero' - the three-digit cap is gone (page limit itself up to 9999, §2023:13.18.39.3 SR5). The subdivision limit stays a syntax rule only for absolute lines and for relative lines ending an absolute group (§2023:13.18.35.3 SR6c, SR6d); a group that cannot fit a page now sets EC-REPORT-PAGE-LIMIT with undefined results (§2023:13.18.35.4 GR2). Looser limits and part of a compile-time refusal moved to a run-time exception condition.
